1.note: This chapter records the names of the people who repaired the wall of Jerusalem, and it describes what parts of the wall they worked on. If it would be helpful in your language, you could say this explicitly at the start of the chapter. (In this book Nehemiah records everything he did to help the people of Judah, and he prays that God will remember him and bless him for what he did. We see in this chapter that he also wants God to remember and bless everyone else who helped.) Alternate translation: [These are the names of the people who helped to rebuild the wall around Jerusalem. Now Eliashib the high priest rose up]
As in 2:18, **rise up** here means to begin something. Alternate translation: [began to]
This is the name of a man. It occurs about a dozen times in the book of Nehemiah. It will be helpful to your readers if you translate it consistently each time.

This means that Eliashib was the leader of the priests who conducted worship in the temple and performed many other religious and community functions. Alternate translation: [the priest who was in charge in the temple]
Here, **brother** could mean Eliashib’s biological brothers, but more likely it refers to the rest of the priests. Alternate translation: [with his fellow priests]

It is clear from the context that they were not building something brand new. Rather, they were rebuilding the walls that had been knocked down. This expression occurs several times in this chapter. It would be helpful to your readers to translate it consistently. Alternate translation: [rebuilt.]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Sheep Gate]

**Consecrate** means to set something apart for a special purpose. The Sheep Gate was the gate closest to the temple. By dedicating it to God, the priests were symbolically dedicating the entire wall to God. The rebuilt wall would define and protect the city of Jerusalem as the place from which God had chosen to start making himself famous throughout the world, as described in 1:9.

If it would be helpful to your readers, you could say explicitly that by dedicating the Sheep Gate to God, the priests were symbolically dedicating the entire wall to God. Alternate translation: [They dedicated this gate to God as a symbolic way of dedicating the entire wall.]

**Its** refers to the Sheep Gate. **Erected** means “set up” or “set in place.” This expression occurs several times in this chapter. It would be helpful to your readers to translate it consistently. Alternate translation: [set the doors in place.]

1.q: וְ⁠עַד־מִגְדַּ֤ל הַ⁠מֵּאָה֙ קִדְּשׁ֔וּ⁠הוּ עַ֖ד מִגְדַּ֥ל חֲנַנְאֵֽל
1.note: In this record of people who helped rebuild the wall, Nehemiah is writing more of a list than a narrative, so he often leaves out one or more words that a sentence normally would have in order to be complete. This sentence seems to mean, “They rebuilt the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred, and beyond that to the Tower of Hananel. Then they dedicated that part of the wall to God as well.” You could say something like that if it would be helpful to your readers.
These are the names of two of the towers on the Jerusalem wall. Alternate translation: [the Tower of the Hundred … the Tower of Hananel]

It is not clear why this tower had this name. The tower could have been 100 cubits high (about 150 feet or about 45 meters), or 100 soldiers may have been stationed there. Since the reason is unknown, it might be best just to call this the “Tower of the Hundred.” However, if it would be confusing to your readers not to explain the meaning of the number, you suggest one of these possibilities. Alternate translation: [The Tower of the Hundred Soldiers] or [The Hundred-Cubit Tower.]

2.note: Here, **at his hand** is a figurative way of saying “beside him” or “next to him.” This expression occurs several times in this chapter. It would be helpful to your readers to translate it consistently. Alternate translation: [next to them]

The word **men** here can include women, and it does seem to include them in this context. Elsewhere in this chapter, 3:12 tells us that “Shallum and his daughters repaired part of the wall.” So we know that both men and women worked on this project. Alternate translation: [people from Jericho]
Jericho is the name of one of the cities in Judah. We see from this chapter that several cities and towns sent work parties to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Zaccur is the name of a man, and Imri is the name of his father.

3.note: Hassenaah is the name of a man.
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Fish Gate]

This expression occurs several times in this chapter. It would be helpful to your readers to translate it consistently. Alternate translation: [They framed it with wooden beams, they set its doors in place, and they installed bolts and bars]
Bolts and bars locked the gates securely. If it would be helpful in your language, you could say this explicitly. Alternate translation: [bolts and bars for locking the gate]

4.note: **Strengthened** means “repaired.” It refers to repairing the wall, although Nehemiah does not specify this. This expression occurs several times in this chapter. It would be helpful to your readers to translate it consistently. Alternate translation: [repaired the next section of the wall]
Meremoth is the name of a man, Uriah is the name of his father, and Hakkoz is the name of his grandfather. Alternate translation: [Meremoth, the son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz]
Meshullam is the name of a man, Berechiah is the name of his father, and Meshezabel is the name of his grandfather. Alternate translation: [Meshullam, the son of Berekiah and grandson of Meshezabel]
Zadok is the name of a man, and Baana is the name of his father.

5.note: These phrases refer to repairing the wall. Alternate translation: [Tekoites repaired the wall]

Tekoa is the name of one of the cities in Judah that sent a work party to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. The Tekoites are the people who came from this city. Alternate translation: [some people from Tekoa]

Here Nehemiah is indicating a contrast between what these people should have done and what they actually did. You can use a word like “but” to indicate this. Alternate translation: [But the leading citizens of Tekoa]
Nehemiah does not state the reason why the nobles did not do the work, but it is implied. Alternate translation: [were too proud to do the work]

Here, the **neck** represents the entire person, and specifically the person at work. The neck is likely associated with work because in this agrarian culture, draft animals would put their necks into yokes so that they could pull plows and drag loads. Alternate translation: [were too proud to do the work]

**Lords** here most likely refers to the leaders of Judah, who had asked all the surrounding cities and towns to send work parties to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. Another possibility is that the plural form of the word “lord” actually refers to God. Alternate translation: [the work that the leaders of Judah had asked them to do] or [the service of their Lord]
**Service** is an abstract noun that refers to the work of rebuilding the wall. You can translate the idea behind it with a concrete noun such as “work.”

6.note: This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Old Gate]
Joiada is the name of a man, and Paseah is the name of his father.
Meshullam is the name of a man, and Besodeiah is the name of his father.

7.note: Melatiah is the name of a man. “Gibeonite” means that he was from the city of Gibeon.
Jadon is the name of a man. “Meronothite” probably means that he was from the town of Meronoth.
Gibeon and Mizpah were two of the cities in Judah that sent work parties to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [other people from Gibeon and from the city of Mizpah]
This is where the governor would have stayed when visiting Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [as far as the residence of the governor of the province Beyond the River]

8.note: Uzziel is the name of a man, and Harhaiah is the name of his father.

This means that Uzziel was one of the goldsmiths who worked in Jerusalem. A goldsmith is a person who makes jewelry and other objects from gold. The term “goldsmith” occurs several more times in the chapter, and if you include both the name and the definition here, that would help your readers understand it in its later occurrences. Alternate translation: [He was one of the goldsmiths, the workers who made jewelry and other objects from gold.]
Hananiah is the name of a man.

**Son of** here is a figurative expression that indicates that a person shares the qualities of something. In this case, the book is describing someone who shares the quality of being a maker of perfume. Alternate translation: [one of the perfumers]

This is the name of one of the features of the Jerusalem wall. This may have been a place where the wall had been built thicker and stronger for strategic purposes. Alternate translation: [They rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall]

9.q: וְ⁠עַל־יָדָ֤⁠ם הֶחֱזִיק֙ רְפָיָ֣ה בֶן־ח֔וּר שַׂ֕ר חֲצִ֖י פֶּ֥לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם
9.note: In this chapter, when Nehemiah names a person, then names their father, and then describes a role, it is the first person, not their father, who was in that role. It will be helpful to your readers if you make this clear. Alternate translation: [Next to them, Rephaiah the son of Hur repaired part of the wall. Rephaiah ruled half of the district of Jerusalem]
Rephaiah is the name of a man, and Hur is the name of his father.

The city of Jerusalem and the surrounding area seem to have been divided into districts for administration. This is the name of one of those districts. Apparently it was so large and populous that it had been further divided into two parts, each with its own administrator. Alternate translation: [ruled half the district of Jerusalem]

10.note: Jedaiah is the name of a man, and Harumaph is the name of his father.
Alternate translation: [repaired the next part of the wall, which was in front his house]
Hattush is the name of a man, and Hashabneiah is the name of his father.

11.note: This expression occurs six times in the chapter. Two of those times, someone who has been named earlier is said to have repaired “a second section,” suggesting, “in addition to the one they did previously.” But the other four times, the people have not been named earlier. So in those cases it might mean “a further section of the wall,” beyond the one just described that someone else worked on. Both of these likely meanings could be accommodated by saying something like “another section of the wall”
Malkijah is the name of a man, and Malkijah is the name of his father.
Hasshub is the name of a man, and Pahath-Moab is the name of his father.
This is the name of one of the towers of the Jerusalem wall. Alternate translation: [the Tower of the Ovens]

12.note: Shallum is the name of a man, and Hallohesh is the name of his father.

This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided. Alternate translation, since the first half has already been named: [Shallum who ruled the other half of the district of Jerusalem]

13.note: This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Valley Gate]
This is the name of a man.
Zanoah is the name of one of the cities in Judah that sent a work party to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the people from Zanoah]
Depending on what would be most helpful to your readers, you could express this either in ancient or modern measurements, “1,000 cubits” or “460 meters” or “1,500 feet.”
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Dung Gate]

14.note: This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Dung Gate]
Malkijah is the name of a man, and Recab is the name of his father.
This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided.

15.note: This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Fountain Gate]
Shallun is the name of a man, and Kol-Hozeh is the name of his father.
This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided.
Alternate translation: [He rebuilt the gate and put a roof over it]
Alternate translation: [the wall that surrounded the Pool of Siloam]
Alternate translation: [next to the royal garden, as far as the steps that went down from the City of David.]
This was one part of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the City of David]

16.note: Nehemiah is the name of a man, and Azbuk is the name of his father. (This is not the same Nehemiah who wrote this book.)
This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided.

16.q: עַד־נֶ֨גֶד֙ קִבְרֵ֣י דָוִ֔יד וְ⁠עַד־הַ⁠בְּרֵכָה֙ הָ⁠עֲשׂוּיָ֔ה וְ⁠עַ֖ד בֵּ֥ית הַ⁠גִּבֹּרִֽים
16.note: Alternate translation: [as far as the place opposite the tombs in the City of David, to the reservoir that the people had made and the army barracks]

17.note: The Levites were descendants of Levi. They had the special assignment of helping the priests. Alternate translation: [Next to him, some Levites repaired parts of the wall.]
Rehum is the name of a man, and Bani is the name of his father.
It seems clear from the context that Rehum was a Levite. If it would be helpful in your language, you could say that explicitly. Alternate translation: [One of them was Rehum the son of Bani.]
Hashabiah is the name of a man.

This does not mean that Hashabiah repaired this part of the wall for the benefit of his district, but rather that he did it leading a work party from his district. Alternate translation: [led a work party from his district that repaired the next section of the wall]
This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided.

18.note: As in [3:1](ta:03), **brother** could mean the biological brothers of the Levites mentioned in 3:17. However, more likely it means other Levites. Alternate translation: [some other Levites repaired more of the wall]

18.q: בַּוַּ֖י בֶּן־חֵנָדָ֑ד שַׂ֕ר חֲצִ֖י פֶּ֥לֶךְ קְעִילָֽה
18.note: Here Nehemiah does not say “at their hand” (next to them) or “strengthened” (repaired another section of the wall). Once again he is leaving out some of what a complete sentence would be expected to contain. you could fill in this information. Alternate translation: [Next to them, Binnui the son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah, repaired more of the wall.]
Binnui is the name of a man, and Henadad is the name of his father.
This is the name of one of the districts into which the city and the surrounding area were divided.

19.note: Ezer is the name of a man, and Jeshua is the name of his father.
Since the district of Mizpah is mentioned in 3:15, this probably means the city of Mizpah. Alternate translation: [Ezer ruled the city of Mizpah]
Alternate translation: [He started from the place in front of the steps that went up to the armory, and he finished at the place where the wall bends slightly.]

20.note: Baruch is the name of a man, and Zabbai is the name of his father.
Here, **burned** is probably a figurative way of saying that Baruch worked with great enthusiasm. You could say that as an alternate translation.

20.q: מִן־הַ֨⁠מִּקְצ֔וֹעַ עַד־פֶּ֨תַח֙ בֵּ֣ית אֶלְיָשִׁ֔יב הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן הַ⁠גָּדֽוֹל
20.note: Alternate translation: [from the bend in the wall as far as the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest]

21.note: Meremoth is the name of a man, Uriah is the name of his father, and Hakkoz is the name of his grandfather. See how you translated these names in 3:4.

21.q: מִ⁠פֶּ֨תַח֙ בֵּ֣ית אֶלְיָשִׁ֔יב וְ⁠עַד־תַּכְלִ֖ית בֵּ֥ית אֶלְיָשִֽׁיב
21.note: Alternate translation: [from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end of his house]

22.note: Jerusalem is up on a mountain, so the area around it would be “the valley.” Alternate translation: [some priests from the area around Jerusalem]

23.note: Alternate translation: [repaired a section opposite their house]
Benjamin and Hasshub are the names of men.
Alternate translation: [repaired the next section, beside his house]
Azariah is the name of a man, Maaseiah is the name of his father, and Ananiah is the name of his grandfather.

24.note: Binnui is the name of a man, and Henadad is the name of his father. See how you translated these names in 3:18.
Alternate translation: [from the house of Azariah to the bend in the wall as far as the bulwark]
Azariah is a man, the same one mentioned in verse 23.

25.note: Palal is the name of a man, and Uzai is the name of his father.

Here again, Nehemiah leaves out some of the words that a sentence would ordinarily need in order to be complete. Alternate translation: [He began at the place opposite the bend in the wall where the watchtower is taller than]
Here, it is likely that **house** means palace, referring to where the king had lived. Alternate translation: [the upper palace of the king]
Alternate translation: [That is near the place where the guards stayed]
Pedaiah is the name of a man, and Parosh is the name of his father.
Once again Nehemiah leaves out some of the words that a sentence would ordinarily need in order to be complete. Alternate translation: [Next to him, Pedaiah the son of Parosh repaired a section]

26.q: וְ⁠הַ֨⁠נְּתִינִ֔ים הָי֥וּ יֹשְׁבִ֖ים בָּ⁠עֹ֑פֶל עַ֠ד נֶ֜גֶד שַׁ֤עַר הַ⁠מַּ֨יִם֙ לַ⁠מִּזְרָ֔ח וְ⁠הַ⁠מִּגְדָּ֖ל הַ⁠יּוֹצֵֽא
26.note: Yet again Nehemiah leaves out some of the words that a sentence would ordinarily need in order to be complete. Alternate translation: [The temple servants who lived on Ophel Hill repaired the wall as far as the eastern side of the Water Gate where there is a tall tower]
The term **Nethinim** describes servants who worked in the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple servants]
This is probably the name of a geographic feature, a fortified extension of the hill that the Jerusalem temple was located on. Alternate translation: [Ophel Hill]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Water Gate]
The phrase refers to a tall tower that juts out from the wall. Alternate translation: [a tall tower]

27.note: Alternate translation: [repaired another section of the wall]

Tekoa is the name of one of the cities in Judah that sent a work party to help rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. The Tekoites were the people who lived there. See how you translated this name in verse 3:5.

27.q: מִ⁠נֶּ֜גֶד הַ⁠מִּגְדָּ֤ל הַ⁠גָּדוֹל֙ הַ⁠יּוֹצֵ֔א וְ⁠עַ֖ד חוֹמַ֥ת הָ⁠עֹֽפֶל
27.note: Alternate translation: [from opposite the very tall watchtower as far as the wall at Ophel Hill]

28.note: This does not mean all the priests. Nehemiah is using the name of the whole group to refer to part of it. Alternate translation: [a group of priests]
The word **above** is used here because the houses of the priests were likely to have been located at a higher elevation than the Horse Gate. Alternate translation: [starting at the Horse Gate]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Horse Gate]
Here **a man** means “each one.” Alternate translation: [Each one repaired the section in front of his own house.]

29.note: Zadok is the name of a man, and Immer is the name of his father.
Shemaiah is the name of a man, and Shecaniah is the name of his father.
Alternate translation: [the person who looked after the East Gate] or [the person who opened and closed the East Gate]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the East Gate]

30.note: Hananiah is the name of a man, and Shelemiah is the name of his father.
Hanun is the name of a man, and Zalaph is the name of his father.
Meshullam is the name of a man, and Berechiah is the name of his father.
Alternate translation: [in front of the rooms where he stayed]

31.note: Malkijah is the name of a man.

As in 3:8, this is a figurative way of saying that Malkijah was one of the goldsmiths. In this figure of speech, the “son of” something shares its qualities. Since the goldsmiths have been mentioned previously (in 3:8, where their work is described), you could say as an alternate translation. Alternate translation: [another one of the goldsmiths]
Alternate translation: [as far as the building used by the temple servants and the merchants]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. “Mustering” refers to soldiers assembling to go out to battle. Alternate translation: [the Mobilization Gate]
Alternate translation: [He built as far as the upper apartments of this building, which were on the corner.]

32.q: וּ⁠בֵ֨ין עֲלִיַּ֤ת הַ⁠פִּנָּה֙ לְ⁠שַׁ֣עַר הַ⁠צֹּ֔אן הֶחֱזִ֥יקוּ
32.note: This brings the description of the repairs back around to where they started. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate this explicitly by saying “the last section.” Alternate translation: [repaired the last section of the wall, from the corner apartments to the Sheep Gate]

This does not mean all the goldsmiths and all the merchants. Nehemiah is once again using the names of whole groups to refer to parts of them. Alternate translation: [some of the other goldsmiths, along with some traders]
This is the name of one of the gates of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [the Sheep Gate]
